predecessors.note: 'Da Qi was formed late in 1130, and the Jin enthroned Liu as its emperor' (Jin-Song wars page): a Jin puppet on land the Jin had overrun. The Jin dossier carries the matching vassal events. There is no Wikipedia article for Da Qi (a red link on the Jin-Song wars page).

minus.text: the Yellow River plain and Shaanxi fought over by Jin, Song and Jin's puppets

predecessors.note: The land of Qi is what the Song still held or contested when the Jin overran it in 1129-1130: the Jin 'eventually captured Kaifeng in early 1130', Zhang Jun held Shaanxi for the Song until he 'was defeated by Wuzhu near Xi'an in late 1130', and 'Da Qi was formed late in 1130' (Jin-Song wars page). Qi's founding event runs before the Song's own late-1130 loss in the compiler's same-year order, so the Song is named as a donor (fx-28); the northern-song_1126 and _1130 keyframes do not overlap (1126-1129, 1130-1138).

successors.note: 'In late 1137, the Jin reduced Liu Yu's title to that of a prince and abolished the state of Qi.' The Jin returned Henan and Shaanxi to the Song in 1139 and retook them in 1140 (Jin page).

capitals.name: Kaifeng
capitals.note: 'Daming in Hebei was the first capital of Qi, before its move to Kaifeng, former capital of the Northern Song' (Jin-Song wars page); the Jin page has Liu Yu at Kaifeng by 1132. Coordinates are the centre of the gazetteer's Kaifeng disc. Daming (1130-1131) is not in the gazetteer and is left out.

rulers.name: Liu Yu
rulers.note: A Song official who defected to the Jin in 1128 (Jin page); enthroned by the Jin in late 1130; reduced to a prince and the state abolished in late 1137.

'Da Qi was formed late in 1130 ... Daming in Hebei was the first capital of Qi, before its move to Kaifeng'. The pages give no boundary: the shape is the Yellow River plain and Shaanxi minus Cliopatria's Southern Song shape of 1139, the reading used in the great-jin dossier (confidence 1).

ledger.note: Late 1130: 'Da Qi was formed late in 1130, and the Jin enthroned Liu as its emperor'; the Jin page: Liu Yu defected in 1128 and was based at Daming. The extent is the researcher's reading (confidence 2); the infobox of the same page gives 'Da Qi (1133-37)'. Repair fx-28 (conflict with northern-song, 2,056 cells in 1130): the Song still held Henan, Shandong and Shaanxi in its ledger when this founding event ran (the Song's loss to the Jin is 'late in 1130'), so northern-song is now a predecessor/donor; the Jin-Song wars page (opened): 'Da Qi was formed late in 1130, and the Jin enthroned Liu as its emperor'; the Jin 'eventually captured Kaifeng in early 1130'; Zhang Jun 'was defeated by Wuzhu near Xi'an in late 1130'.
1132: the capital moves from Daming to Kaifeng ('Daming in Hebei was the first capital of Qi, before its move to Kaifeng'; the Jin page has Liu Yu at Kaifeng by 1132).

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks. The Jin-Song wars page has no article for Da Qi (a red link), so the pages are the Jin-Song wars, Jin, Gaozong and Yue Fei articles; the Da Chu page is silent on Qi.

Extent. No page gives Qi's frontier. The shape is the Yellow River plain (Henan, Shandong) plus Shaanxi minus Cliopatria's Southern Song shape of 1139, as in the great-jin dossier's 1137 gain. Daming (the first capital, in Hebei) is not in the gazetteer, and Hebei is not drawn because the pages do not say how much of it Qi held. Cliopatria's Great Jin shape of 1126 covers none of Henan or Shandong, and its shape of 1139 covers 149 thousand km2 of Henan.

Dates. The Jin-Song wars page says 'late in 1130' and its infobox lists Da Qi as 1133-37; the Jin page has Liu Yu defecting in 1128, at Daming, and at Kaifeng by 1132. Counterpart naming: the great-jin dossier uses 'great-qi' for the vassal pair (1130, 1137) and the 1137 gain; the northern-song dossier uses it for the Xiangyang events.
